name: Daily Scripture Reflection
description: Short passage-led devotional reflections with one grounded practice for daily life.
episode_objects: a selected passage followed by one plainly labeled observation from its wording
a journal prompt and one modest practice tied to the passage's stated concern
a verified verse quotation beside a separate paraphrase of its immediate setting
a closing reflection that labels application as pastoral counsel rather than scripture
time_place_scopes: the passage's literary unit and first-audience setting before modern application
one ordinary present-day decision considered after the passage has been interpreted
the book-level historical context and neighboring verses that limit the reading
a household, workplace, or community moment framed as application rather than original meaning
mechanisms: close reading moves from quoted scripture text to interpretation without merging the two
a bounded application connects the interpreted claim to one voluntary daily practice
genre and immediate context constrain the devotional inference before encouragement begins
reflection distinguishes the passage's claim from the narrator's pastoral response
evidence_lenses: a verified translation with book, chapter, and verse checked before any quotation
literary context notes that identify observation, interpretation, and application separately
first-audience context supported by reputable biblical scholarship without invented citations
cross-passage comparison used only after the primary text's immediate argument is established
exclusions: Do not fabricate scripture quotations, translation wording, chapter-and-verse citations, or scholarly citations.
Keep scripture text or quotation, interpretation, and present-day application visibly separate.
Do not present pastoral encouragement as the only possible exegesis or as a direct quotation from God.
Do not promise healing, prosperity, or a guaranteed outcome from a devotional practice.
prompt_context: Use one passage early and verify any scripture text or quotation against a named translation before citing it. Establish literary and first-audience historical context, label interpretation as interpretation, and only then offer a modest application. Do not fabricate quotations or citations; encouragement follows the text and never impersonates it.
